FTR is a failure to return to a supply or demand.

FTB is when price comes back to supply or demand for the first time.

in my studies I often see price come near a sweet s/d only to reverse
early. This is an FTR - correct? FTR is important when price returns
to the FTR yes? No?

Sorry for my simple mind. I will study more...and more...and....

author: Ifmyante
text:
Very often a zone will break strongly and price will retrace but fail
to retouch it. This is still the FTR - the confirmation of a new trend
(do a study of how price reacts and how far it goes after hitting this
spot). So an FTR can be first time back, but doesn't need to be.

If you ever want to do a study, do it on this

author: Ifmyante
text:
It's Good Friday today, and most of the trading world is on holiday (NY is open, of course).

So it's a good time to write a note on price during holidays.

During holidays, volume in the market is often greatly diminished

This would lead some to imagine that price hardly moves

But

Say someone decided to put a truckload of orders into the market. If
there's nobody else in the market to oppose these orders, price can do
nothing but shoot away.

So remember

Low Volume can = High Volatility

author: Hotochin
text:
Hey IF!

I have a few charts for you to look at. First I have a few observations
though. I have read the homework, watched the videos, and spent several
years trying to teach this to myself. From what I am getting there is a
strong relationship between the diamond, QM, price caps, and triple hit.
 These are all things that can happen at HTF zones. The CORE of what we
are looking for is to find a HTF supply or demand that has history and
been engulfed in one direction or the other. Then we are to zoom down to
 lower time frames and find the precise decision points that price
turned and shot the other direction. These are called swap zones or
decision points, right? When we are looking for decision points on
smaller TF, they can be QM, diamonds, or price caps, right? In the end
we are looking for flag poles on several time frames. Below are some
charts:

The first chart is the 240min. Does it matter if I use the "yellow"
line, or the solid one that the "blue" arrow is pointing to as the price
 that was engulfed on the way up?

Next is the 60 min chart. The solid line is the same line that the
"blue" arrow was pointing to on the 240min. Notice the swap level that
the blue arrow is pointing to.

Next is the 1 minute chart. The dashed line is the higher level from the
 240min chart. Notice the flag that this line makes. Since the base of
the pole is almost engulfed on this one, I rather look at the lower
level. The lower solid line level is the lower level from the 240min
chart. This level seems to also have a swap level that could be the base
 of a flag. That RBR is where I will look to enter. Is this right
thinking?

The last chart is what happened when price returned. Price did not seem
to like that larger flag area that was the higher level on the
240min(price marked with dashed lines). Price did like that lower area
that seemed to be a swap level on the 1min and the base to a flag pole.
Is this thinking correct?

Thanks in advance
